sections.heading: Signs Your Skylight Needs Replacement
sections.body: Skylights are built to last, but they do not last forever. Knowing when to replace rather than repair can save you significant time and money in the long run. Common signs that your skylight has reached the end of its useful life include persistent water intrusion even after resealing, visible condensation or moisture trapped between panes, yellowing or cloudy glazing that blocks natural light, and noticeable drafts around the frame. Cracked or shattered glazing is an obvious red flag, but subtler issues like warped frames, failed flashing, and deteriorating weatherstripping can be just as damaging over time. If you have been patching the same skylight repeatedly without lasting results, a full replacement is likely the more cost-effective solution. Our technicians will assess your existing skylight and give you an honest evaluation so you can make an informed decision for your Chevy Chase property.

sections.heading: Skylight Glazing Options and Materials
sections.body: Not all skylights are created equal, and selecting the right glazing material for your replacement unit depends on your building type, budget, and performance goals. Common options include tempered glass, laminated glass, insulated double-pane glass units, and polycarbonate or acrylic glazing. Each material offers different characteristics in terms of clarity, thermal performance, impact resistance, and longevity. Insulated glazing units, for example, can help reduce heat gain and heat loss compared to single-pane alternatives, which is relevant in Chevy Chase where temperatures vary significantly from summer to winter. Our team can walk you through the available options and help you choose a replacement skylight that suits your property's specific demands. We source quality materials and stand behind the workmanship of every installation we complete.

faq.q: How long does a skylight replacement typically take?
faq.a: Most residential skylight replacements can be completed in a single day, depending on the size and complexity of the unit. Commercial projects or situations involving structural modifications may require additional time. We will give you a clear timeline estimate before work begins.

faq.q: Can you replace just the glass in a skylight, or does the whole unit need to come out?
faq.a: In some cases, only the glazing insert needs to be replaced rather than the entire skylight frame. However, if the frame is warped, corroded, or the flashing has failed, a full unit replacement is usually the better long-term solution. Our technicians will evaluate your specific skylight and recommend the most practical approach.

faq.q: What should I do if my skylight is actively leaking?
